name: Juntong Zhang

papers.title: X-WBC: A Cross-Embodiment Foundation Model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.abstract: Scaling humanoid whole-body control toward general-purpose deployment requires large human motion corpora and training experience shared across robot bodies. Existing methods usually train one policy per robot, leaving motion experience isolated across embodiments. We introduce X-WBC, a cross-embodiment whole-body control foundation framework for diverse humanoid robots. The framework decouples control into relatively embodiment-independent motion representation and embodiment-dependent physical execution. Human motion serves as a natural carrier of motion semantics, learned from multi-robot rollouts through a shared motion backbone, while lightweight robot-specific modules condition execution on each robot's proprioception, dynamics, and action space. To unify heterogeneous control sources, it aligns full human motion, robot reference motion, and sparse VR motion into human-centered command tokens. A causal Transformer with historical context models temporal structure, enabling shared motion understanding across robots. We evaluate X-WBC in simulation on nine humanoid robots with ablations, and deploy it on multiple real robots with substantially different body sizes. Results show that the learned motion representation transfers across robots while maintaining robust execution. These findings support heterogeneous humanoids as joint data sources for WBC training and provide a real-world deployable foundation model for cross-embodiment humanoid whole-body control.
